svg.text: Where the work of a frame runs
Each row: work the draw can do on the GPU thread, where KytyPS5 does it, and what each part is worth in Crash Bandicoot 4
In the draw, on the GPU thread
KytyPS5: ahead, in parallel, or once

g.text: Loading MoltenVK's cache file holds the game's start.
Not kept on disk on MoltenVK
The game's pipeline list is built ahead instead.
Each new shader is translated in its first draw.
About 900 programs in 1.7 s on 4 threads.
frame gaps over 200 ms in 115 s
The draw waits for each new pipeline, up to 1.45 s.
A draw that only changes the picture is left out.
level average on a first run
Per draw, on the GPU thread
The walker interprets the shader's reads per draw.
SRT tape: a flat list of steps
Plans with control flow use the walker.
The same descriptor is decoded on each draw.
Each draw computes its layouts again: 16,800 per frame.
The last 64 layouts kept per thread
A layout depends only on format, size, mips, tiling.
of layout calls answered from them
A table read waits when its page holds any GPU-written byte.
A read waits only for bytes the GPU wrote.
A buffer is made and freed per draw, 0.45 ms each.
Snapshot buffers come from a pool
A run of depth-bounds draws shares one snapshot.
MoltenVK makes each mark a call it never inlines.
Left out where the driver makes them slow
A depth prepass takes about 1 ms, not 9–25 ms.
The game renders at 4K for a 1080p window.
On system memory every image is kept, and MoltenVK
attaches each one to every command buffer.
Images the GPU wrote are kept.
Upload copies and barriers end the pass again and again.
No barrier between read-only uses of an image.
MoltenVK encodes Metal commands on the GPU thread.
MoltenVK encodes on its own thread
The GPU thread records the next draws.
Each guest command buffer is its own Metal one.
A guest wait for GPU-written bytes ends sooner.
Each upload pass uploads the hot ranges again.
A page the game keeps writing faults on every write.
Hot pages stay open for 32 guest frames
One thread copies about 155 MB per frame, 5.6 ms.
Copy workers fill staging in parallel
The ranges of a batch copy at once.
The GPU thread copies them back and waits for all its work.
The thread that asked waits, not the GPU thread.
The first draw on the target reads the GPU's metadata back.
The clear code is read from the guest's fill
No read-back for a fast-cleared target.
